ai.literal: transient things / stable things / that / understanding / petty knowledge quality / lowest
ai.translation: To perceive things that do not last as permanent is the lowest form of ignorance.
ai.modern: நிலைத்து நிற்காத பொருள்களை என்றென்றும் நிலைத்திருப்பவை என்று நம்புகின்ற அற்ப அறிவு மிகவும் கீழானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the worst kind of ignorance as the inability to recognize impermanence. The word நில்லாதவற்றை refers to worldly things like wealth and youth that do not last. Believing them to be நிலையின or permanent shows a petty or shallow understanding, which the poet condemns as the lowest state of mind.

ai.literal: Dance-performance assembly crowd's like-indeed great-wealth departure-too it having-dispersed like
ai.translation: The accumulation of great wealth is like a crowd gathering for a dance performance. Its departure is like that same crowd dispersing.
ai.modern: ஒரு நாடகத்தைக் காண்பதற்காக அரங்கத்தில் கூட்டம் சேர்வதைப் போன்றது பெருஞ்செல்வம் ஒருவனிடம் சேர்வது. அச்செல்வம் அவனை விட்டுப் போவதும், நாடகம் முடிந்த பின் அக்கூட்டம் கலைந்து செல்வதைப் போன்றதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the transient nature of wealth using a vivid simile. Wealth accumulates much like a crowd gathering in a theater to watch a play. Just as the audience naturally disperses once the performance ends, wealth too will eventually leave its possessor. The words 'குழாத்து அற்றே' (like a gathering crowd) and 'விளிந்து அற்று' (like dispersing) perfectly contrast the arrival and departure of riches.

ai.literal: Not-staying nature-it-has wealth; that if obtained, things-that-abide right-then do.
ai.translation: Wealth is transient by nature. When you obtain it, immediately use it to do things that will last.
ai.modern: செல்வம் நிலைக்காத இயல்பினை உடையது. அதனைப் பெற்றால், பெற்ற அப்பொழுதே நிலைத்து நிற்கும் நல்ல செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the fleeting nature of wealth. The word அற்கா means not staying or unstable, describing wealth's natural tendency to vanish. Because wealth can disappear at any moment, the poet advises that the moment one acquires it, they should immediately invest it in அற்குப—deeds of virtue that will endure forever.

ai.literal: Day as one thing like having shown, life sawing sword that, those who understand if obtained.
ai.translation: To those who have the wisdom to understand, what presents itself as a harmless thing called a 'day' is actually a sword that saws away life.
ai.modern: நாள் என்று ஒரு சாதாரணப் பொருளைப் போலத் தன்னைக் காட்டி, உண்மையில் உயிரை அறுக்கும் வாளாகவே காலம் இருக்கிறது என்பதை அறிவுடையவர்கள் உணர்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet exposes the illusion of time. A 'day' (நாள்) appears to be a harmless, ordinary measure of time that we experience one by one. But the poet compares it to a sword (வாள்) that continuously saws (ஈரும்) away at one's life (உயிர்). Only those who deeply understand the transience of the world realize that every passing day is actively cutting their lifespan shorter.

ai.literal: Tongue having choked, hiccup up not-coming before, good deed forward having gone to do is fitting.
ai.translation: Before the tongue is choked and the final gasp rises, one must step forward to do good deeds.
ai.modern: நாக்கு அடைத்துக்கொண்டு மரண விக்கல் எழுவதற்கு முன்பாகவே, முந்திச் சென்று நல்ல செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the suddenness of death and urges immediate action. The phrase 'நாச்செற்று விக்குள்மேல் வாராமுன்' vividly describes the physical signs of approaching death, when the tongue is paralyzed and the final gasp rises. Because life can end abruptly, the poet advises that one should actively step forward to perform good deeds without delay. The emphasis is on the urgency of doing good while one still has the physical capacity.

ai.literal: Yesterday existed a man, today is not, saying greatness possesses this world.
ai.translation: This world possesses the profound greatness of saying, "A man who existed yesterday does not exist today."
ai.modern: நேற்று உயிரோடு இருந்த ஒருவன் இன்று இல்லை என்று சொல்லக்கூடிய நிலையாமையை இந்த உலகம் தன்னுள் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the sudden and absolute transience of human life. The sharp contrast between 'nerunal' (yesterday) and 'iṉṟu' (today) emphasizes how quickly existence turns into non-existence. The word 'perumai' usually means greatness or pride, but here it denotes the profound, awe-inspiring, and inescapable power of the world's impermanence.

ai.literal: Even one moment living they know not; they plan even a crore are not, many.
ai.translation: People do not know if they will live for even another moment, yet the plans they make are not just ten million, but many more.
ai.modern: ஒரு கண நேரம் கூடத் தாங்கள் உயிரோடு வாழ்வோம் என்பதை மனிதர்கள் உறுதியாக அறிய மாட்டார்கள்; ஆனால் அவர்கள் மனதிற்குள் நினைத்துத் திட்டமிடும் காரியங்களோ ஒரு கோடி மட்டுமல்ல, அதற்கும் மேலான பலவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the stark contrast between the fragility of human life and the boundlessness of human ambition. The phrase 'ஒருபொழுதும் வாழ்வது அறியார்' points out that people cannot guarantee their survival for even a single moment. Despite this profound uncertainty, 'கருதுப கோடியும் அல்ல பல' shows that they constantly make countless plans for the future, numbering not just in the millions but far beyond. The poem uses this irony to emphasize the transient nature of life, urging an awareness of mortality over endless worldly planning.

ai.literal: Nest having become alone to be left behind, bird having flown like that indeed, body-with life-between friendship.
ai.translation: The bond between the body and the soul is just like that of a bird that flies away, leaving its empty nest behind.
ai.modern: உடம்பிற்கும் உயிருக்கும் இடையிலான உறவு, பறவை தன் கூட்டினைத் தனியே விட்டுவிட்டுப் பறந்து செல்வதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the transient nature of life using a vivid metaphor. The word 'kuṭampai' can mean either a nest or an egg-shell; in either sense, it represents the physical body left behind. Just as a bird eventually flies away, leaving its former home empty and alone, the soul (uyir) departs from the body (uṭampu) when its time comes. The 'friendship' or bond (naṭpu) between body and soul is temporary, emphasizing that physical existence is not permanent.

ai.literal: Sleeping is-like death; having-slept waking-up is-like birth.
ai.translation: Death is like falling asleep, and birth is like waking up from that sleep.
ai.modern: இறப்பு என்பது தூங்குவதைப் போன்றது; பிறப்பு என்பது தூங்கி விழிப்பதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares the cycle of life and death to the familiar daily cycle of sleeping and waking. Death is likened to the state of sleep, presenting it as a natural and temporary resting phase. Birth is compared to waking up after having slept. This simple analogy emphasizes the transience of life, showing death and birth as alternating, inevitable states rather than absolute endings or beginnings.

ai.literal: Permanent home has not been formed, alas, inside the body in a temporary shelter which stayed to the life.
ai.translation: Alas, has the life that resides in the temporary shelter of the body not yet found a permanent home?
ai.modern: உடம்பாகிய தற்காலிகமான குடிசையில் தங்கியிருக்கும் உயிருக்கு, நிலையான ஒரு வீடு இன்னும் அமையவில்லையோ!
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts a temporary shelter ('tuccil') with a permanent home ('pukkil'). The body is described merely as a temporary, rented corner where life resides for a short time. The poet wonders with pity ('kollō') whether life has not yet found a permanent dwelling, since it keeps moving from one temporary body to another. This highlights the transience of physical existence and the inevitability of death.
